Overview

About the printed a-board sign

A printed A-board is the classic pavement sign: a sturdy steel frame carrying your full-colour printed panels on both sides, so passers-by see your brand from either direction.

  • FrameSteel, silver
  • SizesA2, A1, A0, 20 x 30in, 30 x 40in
  • PrintNone, single or double-sided

Choose from A2, A1, A0, 20 x 30in or 30 x 40in, printed on one side or both. Panels slide into the frame and can be reprinted whenever your offer changes, keeping the frame in use for years.

Placing an A-board on the public pavement may need council permission and must leave room for pedestrians. Browse all pavement signs.

What's included

  • A-board frame
  • Printed panels (if selected)

Good to know

How ordering works

  4. 4Production & deliveryWe make your sign to order, then deliver it or fit it for you across Norfolk and Suffolk.

Installation & fixing

A-boards arrive ready to use: unfold the frame, lock the hinge or stay, and position it outside your door. At the end of the day, fold it flat and bring it inside, which also protects the finish and keeps it secure.

Step by step

Using & caring for your A-board

  1. 01

    Position it

    Place the board close to your entrance, facing the flow of people, leaving plenty of room for wheelchairs and pushchairs.

  2. 02

    Check the rules

    If it stands on the public pavement, check your council's rules or licence conditions.

  3. 03

    Mind the weather

    Bring the board in during high winds and overnight. Swinging and weighted signs cope best with gusts.

  4. 04

    Change your message

    Swap posters or panels, or rewrite chalk and dry-wipe boards, as often as you like to keep passers-by interested.

  5. 05

    Care

    Wipe frames and panels with mild soapy water. Wooden boards last longer when kept dry and brought in at night.

You'll need

  • A clear spot near your door
  • Damp cloth
  • Chalk pens or new posters

Check the pavement rules

Many councils have rules or licences for pavement boards. Keep a clear path for pedestrians, wheelchairs and pushchairs.

Artwork

Artwork guide

Getting your artwork right first time means a sharper sign and a faster turnaround. Here's what we need.

  1. Best file types

    AI · EPS · SVG · PDF

    vector files (AI, EPS, SVG or a PDF exported from design software) give razor-sharp results at any size. High-resolution JPG, PNG or TIFF files work for photos.

  2. Resolution

    150dpi minimum

    for photos and raster images, aim for at least 150dpi at the final printed size (300dpi for small signs viewed close up). Images taken from websites or social media are usually too small.

  3. Colours

    CMYK · Pantone · RAL

    set artwork up in CMYK. If your brand has Pantone or RAL references, tell us and we'll match them as closely as the material allows.

  4. Fonts

    Outlined or embedded

    convert text to outlines or embed fonts in your PDF, so the lettering prints exactly as designed.

  5. Bleed and margins

    3–5mm bleed · 10mm safe area

    add 3 to 5mm bleed around printed panels and keep important text at least 10mm from the edge.

  6. Cut-to-shape signs

    Separate vector cut line

    include the cut line as a separate vector path. If you don't have one, our studio will create it.

Questions

Printed A-Board Sign FAQs

Can't see your question? Call 01603 407786 or send an enquiry.

Can I change the graphics later?

Yes, printed panels can be reprinted when your branding, menu or offer changes.

Which size is best?

A1 suits most shops; A0 or 30 x 40in are better for forecourts and wide pavements.

Do I need a licence for an A-board?

If it stands on the public pavement, many councils require permission or a licence and set rules on size and position. Signs on your own forecourt usually don't need one. Check with your council.

Will it blow over?

Any A-board can move in strong gusts. Place it out of wind tunnels, bring it in during storms, or choose a swinging or weighted-base sign for exposed spots.
